claim: C. elegans has 302 neurons, all of which have been fully mapped on its connectome.
source: C. elegans has 302 neurons, all of which have been fully mapped on its connectome (Cook et al., 2019; White et al., 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research (Cook et al., 2019; White et al., 1986) that documented the complete neural connectome of C. elegans.

claim: C. elegans exhibits chemotaxis to sodium chloride, a phenomenon termed salt chemotaxis.
source: The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans has been demonstrated to exhibit chemotaxis to sodium chloride, a phenomenon termed salt chemotaxis (Ward, 1973).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ward, 1973, which documented salt chemotaxis behavior in C. elegans.

claim: The amphid taste neurons ASE play a crucial role in sensing the concentration of NaCl.
source: In the context of salt chemotaxis, the amphid taste neurons ASE play a crucial role in sensing the concentration of NaCl (Bargmann and Horvitz, 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bargmann and Horvitz, 1991, which identified the role of ASE neurons in NaCl sensing.

claim: ASE sensory neurons consist of two morphologically symmetric neurons on the left (ASEL) and the right (ASER).
source: These sensory neurons, which consist of two morphologically symmetric neurons on the left (ASEL) and the right (ASER), are essential for the detection of alterations in the concentration of NaCl.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text describing the anatomical structure of ASE neurons.

claim: ASER is depolarized by decreases in salt concentration, whereas ASEL responds to increases.
source: These neurons exhibit a functional asymmetry in which the ASER is depolarized by decreases in salt concentration, whereas the ASEL responds to increases (Suzuki et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Suzuki et al., 2008, which characterized the functional asymmetry of ASEL and ASER neurons.

claim: Two distinct behavioral strategies direct C. elegans toward a favorable NaCl concentration during salt chemotaxis: klinokinesis and klinotaxis.
source: Two distinct behavioral strategies that direct C. elegans toward a favorable NaCl concentration during salt chemotaxis have been characterized by an analysis of the migratory behaviors exhibited by the organism (Iino and Yoshida, 2009; Pierce-Shimomura et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Iino and Yoshida, 2009 and Pierce-Shimomura et al., 1999, which characterized these behavioral strategies.

claim: In klinokinesis, the frequency of redirecting turns is increased when the current direction of locomotion is determined to be unfavorable and decreased when it is determined to be favorable.
source: In this strategy, the frequency of redirecting turns is increased when the current direction of locomotion is determined to be unfavorable in relation to the gradient of salt concentration and decreased when it is determined to be favorable (Kunitomo et al., 2013; Pierce-Shimomura et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kunitomo et al., 2013 and Pierce-Shimomura et al., 1999, which described klinokinesis behavior.

claim: In klinotaxis, C. elegans exhibits a continuous turning behavior in a direction that is favorable based on the gradient of salt concentration perpendicular to the direction of locomotion.
source: In this behavioral strategy, C. elegans exhibits a continuous turning behavior in a direction that is favorable based on the gradient of salt concentration perpendicular to the direction of locomotion (Iino and Yoshida, 2009; Kunitomo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Iino and Yoshida, 2009 and Kunitomo et al., 2013, which described klinotaxis behavior.

claim: When well-fed individuals are cultivated at a higher salt concentration than the current environment (Ccult > Ctest), the preferred salt concentrations become higher than the current concentrations.
source: In the presence of food, if the previously cultivated salt concentration is higher than the current environmental concentrations (Ccult > Ctest), the preferred salt concentrations are demonstrated to become higher than the current concentrations (Kunitomo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kunitomo et al., 2013, which demonstrated salt concentration memory-dependent preference behavior.

claim: When well-fed individuals are cultivated at a lower salt concentration than the current environment (Ccult < Ctest), the preferred salt concentrations become lower than the current ambient concentrations.
source: Conversely, if the previously cultivated salt concentration is lower than the current concentrations (Ccult < Ctest), the preferred salt concentrations are demonstrated to become lower than the current ambient concentrations (Kunitomo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kunitomo et al., 2013, which demonstrated salt concentration memory-dependent preference behavior.

claim: The interneuron AIB, postsynaptic to ASER, exhibits a bidirectional response to changes in NaCl concentration dependent on the previously experienced NaCl concentration.
source: The interneuron postsynaptic to the ASER, AIB, which is involved in the behavior of klinokinesis (i.e., the redirecting turn), exhibits a bidirectional response to changes in NaCl concentration in the current environment, dependent on the previously experienced NaCl concentration (Sato et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sato et al., 2021, which characterized the bidirectional response of AIB neurons.

claim: The bidirectional neural responses of AIB are mediated by a change in the basal level of glutamate neurotransmitter released from ASER.
source: The bidirectional neural responses have been demonstrated to be mediated by a change in the basal level of glutamate neurotransmitter released from the ASER (Sato et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sato et al., 2021, which demonstrated the mechanism of bidirectional responses.

claim: The alteration in basal glutamate transmission results in a bidirectional response of postsynaptic AIB due to the distinct sensitivities of the excitatory glutamate receptor GLR-1 and the inhibitory glutamate receptor AVR-14.
source: The alteration in the basal glutamate transmission results in a bidirectional response of the postsynaptic AIB due to the distinct sensitivities of the excitatory glutamate receptor GLR-1 and the inhibitory glutamate receptor AVR-14, which are expressed on the AIB (Hiroki et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hiroki et al., 2022, which elucidated the mechanism of bidirectional responses involving glutamate receptors.

claim: AIY plays a crucial role in initiating the curving turn by forming an inhibitory synapse with AIZ.
source: Specifically, it was demonstrated that the AIY plays a crucial role in initiating the curving turn by forming an inhibitory synapse with the AIZ (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2014, which demonstrated the inhibitory synaptic connection between AIY and AIZ.

claim: The inhibitory synaptic transmission from AIY to AIZ is induced when the Cl− ion channel of the acetylcholine receptor ACC-2 on postsynaptic AIZ is activated by ACh released from presynaptic AIY.
source: Indeed, it was observed that the inhibitory synaptic transmission is induced when the Cl− ion channel of the acetylcholine (ACh) neurotransmitter receptor, ACC-2, on the postsynaptic AIZ is activated by the ACh neurotransmitter released from the presynaptic AIY (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2014, which characterized the mechanism of inhibitory synaptic transmission.

claim: The most optimized model with constraints had a chemotaxis index (CI) of 0.877.
source: The CI values for the most optimized networks with and without the neurophysiological constraints were 0.877 and 0.855, respectively, as shown in Figure 2.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the evolutionary algorithm optimization presented in Figure 2.

claim: The most optimized model without constraints had a chemotaxis index (CI) of 0.855.
source: The CI values for the most optimized networks with and without the neurophysiological constraints were 0.877 and 0.855, respectively, as shown in Figure 2.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the evolutionary algorithm optimization presented in Figure 2.

claim: The constrained model exhibited a marginally accelerated attainment of the salt concentration peak compared to the unconstrained model.
source: The difference between these CI values is slight, while the model optimized with the constraints exhibits a marginally accelerated attainment of the salt concentration peak, as shown by the trajectories.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of trajectories shown in Figure 2.

claim: The evolutionary search with constraints successfully yielded a network with inhibitory AIY–AIZ synaptic connections as the most optimized model.
source: As illustrated in Figure 3b, the evolutionary search with the constraints successfully yielded the network with inhibitory AIY–AIZ synaptic connections as the most optimized model.
evidence: The claim is supported by the network structure shown in Figure 3b resulting from the evolutionary algorithm.

claim: The ASER–AIY synaptic connections in the constrained model are inhibitory.
source: A noteworthy distinction between Figure 3a and b is that the ASER–AIY synaptic connections in the constrained model are inhibitory (Figure 3b) whereas those in the unconstrained model are excitatory (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the network structure shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The ASER–AIY synaptic connections in the unconstrained model are excitatory.
source: A noteworthy distinction between Figure 3a and b is that the ASER–AIY synaptic connections in the constrained model are inhibitory (Figure 3b) whereas those in the unconstrained model are excitatory (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the network structure shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The constrained model reproduces the pattern of neuronal activity observed in experiments where ASER and AIZ activation are synchronized.
source: This indicates that the model reproduces the pattern of neuronal activity observed in the experiments.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison between model results (Figure 3d) and experimental observations cited from Matsumoto et al., 2024.

claim: The unconstrained model exhibited a hyperpolarization of AIZs in response to a decrease in salt concentration.
source: In contrast, the unconstrained model exhibited an inverse activity pattern of AIZs, namely, a hyperpolarization of AIZs, in response to a decrease in the salt concentration (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by the neurotransmitter release patterns shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The positive correlation between the curving rate and the bearing indicates that the model worm continuously turns in the direction of the steepest increase in salt concentration.
source: The positive correlation between the curving rate and the bearing, as illustrated in Figure 4a, indicates that the model worm continuously turns in the direction of the steepest increase in salt concentration (see Figure 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis of curving rate versus bearing shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The positive correlation between the curving rate and the normal gradient of salt concentration indicates that the model worm is able to sense the concentration gradient normal to the travel direction and thus turn in the direction that increases the salt concentration.
source: The positive correlation between the curving rate and the normal gradient of the salt concentration, as illustrated in Figure 4c, indicates that the model worm is able to sense the concentration gradient normal to the travel direction and thus turn in the direction that increases the salt concentration.
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis of curving rate versus normal gradient shown in Figure 4c.

claim: When the basal level of glutamate release from ASER is nearly comparable to the EC50 for GLC-3, the activity of MGL-1 is saturated so that MGL-1 does not contribute to a change in the membrane potential of AIY upon depolarization of ASER.
source: In the case of Ccult > Ctest, if the basal level of glutamate release from the ASER is nearly comparable to the level of EC50 for the GLC-3, the activity of MGL-1 is saturated so that the MGL-1 does not contribute to a change in the membrane potential of the AIY upon the depolarization of the ASER (for more details regarding the release of internal Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum, see, e.g., the reference on a metabotropic acetylcholine receptor; Sumi and Harada, 2023).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from known receptor properties and supported by a citation to Sumi and Harada, 2023.

claim: When the basal level of glutamate release from ASER is sufficiently lower than the EC50 for GLC-3 but nearly comparable to the EC50 for MGL-1, the synaptic transmissions between ASER and AIY become excitatory as a result of Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum mediated by activation of MGL-1.
source: Conversely, in the case of Ccult < Ctest, when the basal level of glutamate release from the ASER is sufficiently lower than the level of EC50 for the GLC-3 but still nearly comparable to the level of EC50 for the MGL-1, the synaptic transmissions between the ASER and the AIY become excitatory as a result of the Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum, which is mediated by the activation of MGL-1 (Ashida et al., 2019; Shidara et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from receptor properties and supported by citations to Ashida et al., 2019 and Shidara et al., 2013.

claim: The most optimized network with constraints, in which only the inhibitory connections between ASER and AIY were replaced by excitatory connections, can reproduce the salt preference behavior of a well-fed individual cultivated at a lower salt concentration than the current environment.
source: These findings are consistent with the experimental observation shown in Figure 5d, indicating that the most optimized network with the constraints, of which only the inhibitory connections between ASER and AIY were replaced by excitatory connections (Figure 5b), can reproduce the salt preference behavior of a well-fed individual cultivated at a lower salt concentration than the current environment.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of model results (Figure 5c) with experimental data (Figure 5d).

claim: The inhibition of SMB activity by reducing the strength of synaptic connections between AIZ and SMB resulted in the suppression of salt preference behavior.
source: Figure 6b shows that the inhibition of the SMB activity by reducing the strength of synaptic connections between AIZ and SMB resulted in the suppression of salt preference behavior, which is consistent with the experimental observations presented in Figure 6a.
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 6b and comparison with experimental data in Figure 6a.

claim: The inhibition of SMB function through the reduction of bias terms in the SMB motor neurons resulted in the suppression of the salt preference behavior.
source: Moreover, the inhibition of SMB function through the reduction of bias terms in the SMB motor neurons resulted in the suppression of the salt preference behavior (see Figure 6—figure supplement 1b), which is a comparable result to that shown in Figure 6b and is also consistent with the experimental data presented in Figure 6a or Figure 6—figure supplement 1a; Kunitomo et al., 2013.
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1b and comparison with experimental data.

claim: The inhibitory synaptic connections between ASER and AIY are essential for synchronizing the activation of AIZs with the activity of ASER, provided that the AIY–AIZ connections are inhibitory.
source: The inhibitory connections between ASER and AIYs are essential for synchronizing the activation of AIZs with the activity of ASER, provided that the AIY–AIZ connections are inhibitory, as has been identified through experiments. (Li et al., 2014; Matsumoto et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results and supported by citations to Li et al., 2014 and Matsumoto et al., 2024.

claim: The salt concentration memory is encoded as a basal level of glutamate release from ASER.
source: These findings indicate that the salt concentration memory is encoded as a basal level of glutamate release from the ASER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results and experimental observations.

claim: The memory encoded as basal glutamate release is decoded by the difference in the sensitivity of the glutamate-gated inhibitory channel GLC-3 and the excitatory metabotropic glutamate receptor MGL-1 expressed on AIY.
source: This memory is then decoded by the difference in the sensitivity of the glutamate-gated inhibitory channel GLC-3 (Ohnishi et al., 2011) and the excitatory metabotropic glutamate receptor MGL-1 (Kang and Avery, 2009), which are expressed on the AIY.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from receptor properties and supported by citations to Ohnishi et al., 2011 and Kang and Avery, 2009.

claim: The circuit downstream of ASE functions as a module that is responsible for salt klinotaxis.
source: The neural network, derived from the hypothesis, reproduced the salt concentration memory-dependent preference behavior and revealed that the circuit downstream of ASE functions as a module that is responsible for salt klinotaxis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results showing that downstream neurons do not undergo alterations and simply transmit signals.

claim: The sensorimotor circuit allows a simple and efficient bidirectional regulation of salt preference behavior in klinotaxis.
source: Consequently, the sensorimotor circuit allows a simple and efficient bidirectional regulation of salt preference behavior in klinotaxis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results showing synaptic plasticity at ASER-AIY enables bidirectional regulation.

claim: The worms are capable of efficiently switching between dwelling and dispersing behaviors by activating or inhibiting only the most downstream motor neurons in the sensorimotor circuit of klinotaxis depending on the presence or absence of food.
source: These findings indicate that the worms are capable of efficiently switching between dwelling and dispersing behaviors by activating or inhibiting only the most downstream motor neurons in the sensorimotor circuit of klinotaxis depending on the presence or absence of food.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results showing SMB inhibition suppresses salt preference behavior.

claim: The principle of operation, in which the dependence of motor responses to sensory inputs on the phase of motor oscillation, appears to be a convergent solution for taxis and navigation across species.
source: The principle of operation, in which the dependence of motor responses to sensory inputs on the phase of motor oscillation, appears to be a convergent solution for taxis and navigation across species.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from observations in multiple species and supported by citations to studies in Drosophila and zebrafish.

claim: Analogous mechanisms to the regulatory mechanism of turning angle have been postulated in the context of chemotaxis in Drosophila larvae and phototaxis in zebrafish.
source: In fact, analogous mechanisms have been postulated in the context of chemotaxis in Drosophila larvae chemotaxis (Wystrach et al., 2016) and phototaxis in zebrafish (Wolf et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wystrach et al., 2016 and Wolf et al., 2017.

claim: The basal level of glutamate release from ASER either increased or decreased when well-fed individuals were cultivated at either a higher or lower salt concentration than the current environment, respectively.
source: In the previous studies on the salt concentration memory-dependent bidirectional regulation of klinokinesis (i.e., pirouettes), it was demonstrated that the basal level of glutamate release from the ASER either increased or decreased when well-fed individuals were cultivated at either a higher or lower salt concentration than the current environment, respectively (Hiroki et al., 2022; Sato et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hiroki et al., 2022 and Sato et al., 2021.

claim: When the cultivated salt concentration exceeds the current environmental concentrations (Ccult > Ctest), the basal glutamate release from ASER is enhanced by the phosphorylation of UNC-64/Syntaxin 1A at Ser65 through the protein kinase C (PKC-1) signaling pathway.
source: When the cultivated salt concentration exceeds the current environmental concentrations (Ccult > Ctest), the basal glutamate release from the ASER is enhanced by the phosphorylation of UNC-64/Syntaxin 1A at Ser65 through the protein kinase C (PKC-1) signaling pathway (Hiroki et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hiroki et al., 2022.

claim: In the case of Ccult < Ctest, the basal glutamate release is decreased as a consequence of the reduced PKC-1 activity.
source: Conversely, in the case of Ccult < Ctest, the basal glutamate release is decreased as a consequence of the reduced PKC-1 activity (Hiroki et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hiroki et al., 2022.

claim: The EC50 for GLC-3 has been reported to be 1.9 mM.
source: The EC50 for GLC-3 has been reported to be 1.9 mM (Horoszok et al., 2001), while the EC50 for MGL-1 is not available in the literature.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Horoszok et al., 2001.

claim: The EC50 for the C. elegans homolog of MGL-1, MGL-2, has been reported to be 9 µM.
source: On the other hand, the EC50 for the C. elegans homolog of MGL-1, MGL-2, has been reported to be 9 µM (Tharmalingam et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tharmalingam et al., 2012.

claim: The sensitivity of MGL-2 is ~200 times higher than that of GLC-3.
source: The sensitivity of MGL-2 is ~200 times higher than that of GLC-3, suggesting that the sensitivity of MGL-1 may also be sufficiently higher than that of GLC-3.
evidence: The claim is based on calculation from reported EC50 values.

claim: At least two glutamate receptors are expressed in AIY: the inhibitory glutamate-gated chloride anion channel GLC-3 and the excitatory metabotropic glutamate receptor MGL-1.
source: At least two glutamate receptors, the inhibitory glutamate-gated chloride anion channel GLC-3 (Ohnishi et al., 2011) and the excitatory metabotropic glutamate receptor MGL-1 (Kang and Avery, 2009), have been demonstrated to be expressed in the AIY, the postsynaptic interneuron to the ASER.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ohnishi et al., 2011 and Kang and Avery, 2009.

claim: GLR-1 is a glutamate-gated cation channel.
source: The GLR-1 is a glutamate-gated cation channel, whereas the AVR-14 is a glutamate-gated chloride anion channel.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about receptor properties.

claim: AVR-14 is a glutamate-gated chloride anion channel.
source: The GLR-1 is a glutamate-gated cation channel, whereas the AVR-14 is a glutamate-gated chloride anion channel.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about receptor properties.

claim: The sensitivity of GLR-1 (EC50 5 mM) is several tens of times lower than that of AVR-14 (EC50 0.2 mM).
source: In addition, the sensitivity of GLR-1 (EC50 5 mM) is several tens of times lower than that of the AVR-14 (EC50 0.2 mM) (Hiroki et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hiroki et al., 2022.

claim: In the absence of food, the PDE neurons do not release dopamine, which causes AVK interneurons that form inhibitory connections with the PDE to release FLP-1 neuropeptides that inhibit SMB motor neurons.
source: In the absence of food, the PDE neurons do not release dopamine, which causes AVK interneurons that form inhibitory connections with the PDE to release FLP-1 neuropeptides that inhibit SMB motor neurons.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about the neural pathway.

claim: The release of FLP-1 neuropeptides that inhibit SMB motor neurons has been postulated to contribute to the dispersal behavior observed in starved individuals.
source: This has been postulated to contribute to the dispersal behavior observed in starved individuals (Oranth et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Oranth et al., 2018.

claim: The neuroanatomical minimal circuit was derived from the connectome by applying two constraints.
source: The neuroanatomical minimal circuit was derived from the connectome by applying two constraints (Izquierdo and Beer, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Izquierdo and Beer, 2013.

claim: The first constraint is to minimize the path length between ASE and SMB cells, resulting in a minimum number of three.
source: The first constraint is to minimize the path length between ASE and SMB cells, resulting in a minimum number of three.
evidence: The claim describes a methodological constraint used in deriving the minimal circuit.

claim: The second step is to eliminate the interneurons that are connected by neuronal connections other than those with the maximum number of contacts.
source: The second step is to eliminate the interneurons that are connected by neuronal connections other than those with the maximum number of contacts (Oshio, 2003).
evidence: The claim describes a methodological constraint and is supported by a citation to Oshio, 2003.

claim: The two interneurons AIY and AIZ, which have been experimentally shown to be involved in klinotaxis, are included in the resulting minimal network.
source: It is noteworthy that the two interneurons, AIY (Kocabas et al., 2012) and AIZ (Iino and Yoshida, 2009), which have been experimentally shown to be involved in klinotaxis, are included in the resulting minimal network.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kocabas et al., 2012 and Iino and Yoshida, 2009.

claim: A similar inhibitory synaptic transmission to AIY due to the influx of Cl− via GLC-3, which is activated by glutamate signals from the AFD sensory neurons, has been demonstrated in the context of thermotaxis in C. elegans.
source: The argument presented here is also supported by evidence that a similar inhibitory synaptic transmission to the AIY due to the influx of Cl− via the GLC-3, which is activated by glutamate signals from the AFD sensory neurons, has been demonstrated in the context of thermotaxis in C. elegans (Ohnishi et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ohnishi et al., 2011.
